## `virtualization.hypervisor`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A virtualization layer that manages one or more virtual machines. Analogous to a hypervisor in any cloud or on-premises virtualization environment.

**Type:** `virtualization.hypervisor`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | [`virtualization.hypervisor.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the hypervisor instance. [1] | `3931-45A01/ZVM1`; `4c4c4544-0042-3510-8058-b4c04f4e3732` |
| Description | [`virtualization.hypervisor.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the hypervisor. | `active`; `inactive`; `unknown` |
| Description | [`virtualization.hypervisor.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The type of hypervisor controlling the virtual machines. [2] | `type1`; `type2`; `unknown` |
| Description | [`virtualization.hypervisor.version`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-version) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The version string of the hypervisor software. [3] | `6.4.0`; `2024.1.1`; `4.2.1-release` |
| Description | [`virtualization.system.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-system-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [4] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[1] `virtualization.hypervisor.id`:** Uniquely identifies the hypervisor instance across the management domains in which it is observed.
- IBM z/VM: the z/VM system name qualified by the CPC
  (`virtualization.platform.id`), e.g. `3931-45A01/ZVM1`.
- VMware vSphere: the ESXi host hardware UUID. - KVM / libvirt: the libvirt host UUID.

**[2] `virtualization.hypervisor.type`:** Classifies the hypervisor by its position in the virtualization stack. Type-1 (bare-metal) hypervisors run directly on hardware; Type-2 (hosted) hypervisors run within a host operating system.

**[3] `virtualization.hypervisor.version`:** The version as reported by the hypervisor software itself. Format is hypervisor-specific and should be used for informational purposes and correlation with vendor release notes.

**[4] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology in use. This attribute allows consumers to correlate platform-specific behaviour and capabilities when multiple virtualization technologies are observed in a mixed environment. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

## `virtualization.partition`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A hardware or firmware enforced partition of a virtualization platform. Analogous to a virtual machine or cloud instance, but enforced at the firmware level rather than by a software hypervisor.

**Type:** `virtualization.partition`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Identity | [`virtualization.platform.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-platform-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the virtualization platform. [6] | `3931-45A01`; `4c4c4544-0042-3510-8058-b4c04f4e3732` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the partition. [7] | `LPAR1`; `PROD`; `LINUX01` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.number`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-number) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The partition number assigned by the virtualization platform. [8] | `1`; `2`; `15` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the partition. [9] | `active`; `not_activated`; `stopped` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The workload type or operational mode of the partition. [10] | `general_purpose`; `linux_only`; `ssc` |
| Description | [`virtualization.system.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-system-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [11] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[5] `virtualization.partition.id`:** Identifies the partition within its virtualization platform (`virtualization.platform.id`); the pair identifies it globally. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the partition. On IBM Z and LinuxONE this is the logical partition (LPAR) name, which the HMC Web Services API, z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 `SMF70LPM`) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo` `LPAR Name`) all report.

**[6] `virtualization.platform.id`:** Identifies the physical computing platform. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the platform and MUST NOT change during its lifetime, so names and management-tool internal object IDs are not used.
- IBM Z and LinuxONE: `<machine type>-<serial number>` of the Central
  Processing Complex (CPC), with leading zeros removed from the serial,
  e.g. `3931-45A01`. The HMC Web Services API (CPC `machine-type`,
  `cpc-serial-number`), z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 `SMF70CPC_TYPE`,
  `SMF70CSC`) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo` `Type`,
  `Sequence Code`) all report it.
- VMware vSphere: the ESXi host hardware UUID. - KVM / libvirt: the host machine ID.
Equal to `host.id` of the same platform.

**[7] `virtualization.partition.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface, e.g., the HMC (Hardware Management Console) for IBM Z PR/SM partitions. On IBM Z, partition names are 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters.

**[8] `virtualization.partition.number`:** The numeric index identifying the partition within the platform. On IBM Z PR/SM (classic) mode, this corresponds to the LPAR number as reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[9] `virtualization.partition.state`:** Reflects the current activation or execution state of the partition as reported by the virtualization platform management interface.

**[10] `virtualization.partition.type`:** Classifies the partition by the category of workload it is configured to run. On IBM Z, this maps to the partition type field on the HMC.

**[11] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the virtualization technology managing this partition. Use this attribute to discriminate partition metrics by platform — e.g. filter on "ibm.prsm" to isolate IBM Z LPAR metrics from generic virtualization partition metrics.

**[12] `virtualization.platform.id`:** Stable and identical for every observer of the platform; see the attribute definition for how each platform fills it (IBM Z: `<machine type>-<serial number>` of the CPC).

**[13] `host.arch`:** The CPU architecture of the platform. SHOULD be set to "s390x" for IBM Z and LinuxONE systems.

**[14] `host.id`:** SHOULD be equal to `virtualization.platform.id`, so consumers that use only the generic host entity identify the same platform.

**[15] `host.name`:** The name of the physical computing platform as configured in the platform management interface. For IBM Z systems this is the CPC name as configured on the Hardware Management Console (HMC). Descriptive only: a platform can be renamed without becoming a different platform.

**[16] `host.type`:** The hardware model of the physical platform. For IBM Z systems this is the machine type and model concatenated with a hyphen, e.g., "9175-ME1" for the IBM z16 Model ME1. Consumers that use only the generic host entity should prefer host.type over virtualization.platform.model.

**[17] `virtualization.platform.firmware.version`:** The firmware or microcode version as reported by the platform management interface. For IBM Z this corresponds to the driver or MCL level reported by the HMC. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

**[18] `virtualization.platform.serial_number`:** The hardware serial number as reported by the platform management interface.

**[19] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology managing this platform (e.g. ibm.prsm, ibm.zvm, vmware.esxi).

**[20] `virtualization.platform.model`:** The model identifier of the platform hardware. Consumers should prefer host.type; this attribute is retained for implementations that need the platform-specific model string separately.

**[21] `virtualization.platform.name`:** The human-readable name as configured in the platform management interface. Consumers should prefer host.name as the name attribute; this attribute is retained for compatibility with implementations that populate both.

## `virtualization.resource_pool`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A hierarchical boundary that controls CPU shares, memory reservations, and capacity limits for the virtual machines or partitions it contains. Analogous to a VMware vSphere Resource Pool, a Kubernetes Namespace ResourceQuota, or an IBM Z PR/SM Shared Processor Pool.

**Type:** `virtualization.resource_pool`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Description | [`virtualization.resource_pool.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-resource-pool-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the virtualization resource pool. [23] | `high-priority-pool`; `linux-pool`; `Default Shared Pool` |
| Description | [`virtualization.system.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-system-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [24] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[22] `virtualization.resource_pool.id`:** Resource pool names are not unique across management domains; see the attribute definition for how each platform fills the identifier.

**[23] `virtualization.resource_pool.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface. For VMware vSphere this is the resource pool name in vCenter. For IBM Z PR/SM this corresponds to the shared processor pool name as reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[24] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the virtualization technology owning this resource pool. Filter on "ibm.prsm" to isolate IBM Z shared processor pool metrics.

---

`virtualization.system.name` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hyperv` | Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ibm.powervm` | IBM PowerVM hypervisor for IBM Power Systems. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ibm.prsm` | IBM PR/SM (Processor Resource/System Manager) Type-1 hypervisor for IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ibm.zvm` | IBM z/VM hypervisor running on IBM Z hardware. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `kubevirt` | KubeVirt — a Kubernetes extension that enables running virtual machines (VMs) as Kubernetes workloads, using KVM under the hood. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `kvm` | Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) — a Type-1 hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, commonly used with QEMU for full virtualisation on x86 and IBM Z (KVM on z Systems) hardware. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `openshift_virtualization` | OpenShift Virtualization — Red Hat's enterprise distribution of KubeVirt integrated into OpenShift Container Platform, managing VMs as first-class Kubernetes resources. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Virtualization system is not known. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `virtualbox` | Oracle VirtualBox hosted hypervisor. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `vmware.esxi` | VMware ESXi bare-metal hypervisor. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `vmware.workstation` | VMware Workstation hosted hypervisor. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `xen` | Xen open-source hypervisor. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
